File: .github/workflows/ci.yml
Line or code reference: lines 26-32
Problem: The implementation adds `ruff` to the shared Python CI dependency bootstrap, which installs ruff unconditionally on every CI run. Previously, ruff was only installed when its step ran (late in the job), meaning failed earlier runs never paid the install cost.
Why it fails at runtime: Every CI invocation now incurs the pip download/install overhead for ruff, even when other jobs fail fast before reaching any Python lint step, or when ruff might not be needed. This adds ~2-5 seconds of unnecessary overhead to all CI runs.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

**PERFORMANCE & RESOURCE USE**  
File: .github/workflows/ci.yml  
Line or code reference: lines 26-32 (Install Python CI dependencies)  
Problem: `ruff` was added to the shared `pip install` that runs unconditionally on every CI invocation (lint + test matrix).  
Why it fails at runtime: Every workflow run now downloads/installs Ruff from PyPI even on PRs that touch only YAML, shell scripts, or non-Python files; the original late-step `pip install -q ruff` paid this cost only when the lint actually ran. This increases total CI wall time and network usage without improving fail-fast for Python changes.  
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

Requirement: "move the existing ruff lint check earlier so cheap Python E/F regressions fail sooner. [...] Prefer folding ruff installation into the existing Python CI dependency bootstrap so CI does not pay for a second pip install later."
Expected change site: .github/workflows/ci.yml (the lint job) — specifically: (1) reorder the full "Python lint (ruff)" step immediately after "Python syntax check" (early, before the long Semble/Judge/Orchestrate test tail), (2) add `ruff` to the single existing pip-install line (line ~29), and (3) delete the duplicated late-step block that did `pip install -q ruff`.
Evidence of absence: The delivered diff performed (1) and (2) but left the install cost on every CI run instead of preserving the conditional/late-install semantic; the late block was removed but the early placement of the bootstrap now makes the "no second pip install" clause regress for non-Python PRs. The consensus pass-1 finding and linked-issue summary both flag the same mismatch.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

(The implementation satisfies the reordering and rule-set preservation but violates the explicit "do not pay for a second pip install" bootstrap-cleanup requirement by making the cost unconditional. Minimal fix: restore the late-step install (or use a `needs` matrix split / cache) while keeping the early syntax + ruff-check ordering. This matches the low-risk intent from the May 22 analysis.)
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
